title: Comparison criteria and the asterisk
summary: Use greater than, less than and not equal to, and the asterisk to match part of a text, in COUNTIF and SUMIF criteria.
intro:
The criterion in `COUNTIF` and `SUMIF` can be a comparison written between quotation marks: `"<20"` means less than 20, `">=20"` means 20 or more, and `"<>Bread"` means not equal to "Bread".

The asterisk `*` means "any text", so the criterion `"T*"` matches every word that starts with T.

faq.q: How do I write "greater than or equal to"?
faq.a: Type `">="` and then the number, such as `">=100"`, with the greater-than sign before the equals sign.

faq.q: What does the asterisk mean in a criterion?
faq.a: It stands for any number of characters, so `"T*"` matches "Tea" and "Tahini".

less-than.prompt: A criterion can be a comparison between quotation marks. In `F2`, type the formula `=COUNTIF(B2:B7,"<20")` to count the products with less than 20 in stock.

greater-or-equal.prompt: In `F3`, write a formula that adds up the stock of the products with 20 or more in stock.
greater-or-equal.hint: If the range to add is the same as the criterion range, you don't need the third argument.

not-equal.prompt: The sign `<>` means "not equal to". In `F4`, write a formula that counts the products that are not "Bread".

greater-than-prices.prompt: In `F5`, write a formula that adds up the prices of the products that cost more than 4.

wildcard.prompt: The asterisk `*` in a criterion means "any text". In `F6`, write a formula that counts the products whose name starts with "T": `=COUNTIF(A2:A7,"T*")`.

which-criterion.prompt: Which criterion counts the values greater than or equal to 100?
